subject: Finovate: renewal timing and convenience-termination carveouts in MSA / Order Form
messages:
From: Jill Park <procurement@finovate.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Finovate Legal <legal@finovate.com>
Date: 2026-10-31T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify renewal mechanics & termination-for-convenience carveout

Neha — thanks for the call earlier. I attached Finovate's redline to the MSA and the draft Order Form for your review (Finovate_MSA_redline_v1.docx, OrderForm_Draft.pdf). A couple of items we need clarity on before procurement can sign: 

- Auto-renew: we cannot accept open-ended auto-renewals without a clear opt-out window. We typically require a 90-day notice window to opt out of renewal for enterprise contracts.
- Termination for convenience: for pilot and short-term engagements we can accept 30–60 days, but for enterprise / committed capacity we need a termination-for-convenience right with a 60-day notice and a pro-rata refund for any prepaid service credits.

Can you confirm Redwood's flexibility on those two points and whether you can offer a documented path for migration/hand-off if Finovate exercises termination for convenience? Procurement is also asking whether there will be a termination fee or any non-cancellable minimums tied to reserved capacity.

Goal: get to a mutually acceptable redline we can circulate to our legal team this week.

Thanks,
Jill Park
Head of Procurement — Finovate Inc.
procurement@finovate.com

--- Attachment: Finovate_MSA_redline_v1.docx (redline, 2 pages)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jill Park <procurement@finovate.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-31T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify renewal mechanics & termination-for-convenience carveout

Hi Jill — appreciate the clear note and the redline. Quick responses to each ask and proposed compromise so we have something concrete for your legal team: 

- Auto-renew: Redwood's standard is 12-month term with annual auto-renew unless either party gives notice. We're generally flexible on the notice window for enterprise customers. For Finovate I can offer a 60-day opt-out window for annual renewals (instead of our standard 30 days) if the Order Form is for a 12-month committed term.

- Termination for convenience: for pilots / short-term engagements (<$50k ARR) we can allow a 30-day termination for convenience with pro-rata refunds. For enterprise commitments (>= $50k ARR or reserved capacity), we typically require a 90-day notice or a termination fee to cover reserved capacity provisioning. That said, I'm prepared to propose a middle ground: allow termination for convenience with 60 days' notice and either (a) pro-rata refund of unused prepaid months minus an administrative processing fee, or (b) option to transition to pay-as-you-go for remaining months at list pricing (whichever is lower for Finovate).

Operationally, we will include a transition runbook (data export, KV cache handoff steps, and a one-week dedicated runbook call) for any convenience termination of enterprise engagements.

Looping in Laura (sales ops) and Marcus (billing) to confirm operational constraints. I'm also going to ask legal to produce a short clause we can bake into the Order Form so your counsel has something to react to.

If this looks close, share the earliest signature target and we'll aim to get a DocuSign-ready Order Form.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

--- Attachment: OrderForm_Draft.pdf (1 page)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jill Park <procurement@finovate.com>, Finovate Legal <legal@finovate.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Clarify renewal mechanics & termination-for-convenience carveout — proposed legal language

Team / Jill — I reviewed Finovate's redline and Neha's compromise. Below is a short, negotiable clause set we can propose that captures the operational protections Redwood needs while addressing Finovate's procurement concerns. I've attached an annotated draft: MSA_redline_karthik_v2.docx. Key points: 

1) Auto-Renewal / Notice Window (Order Form): 
   - "Unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Term, the Term shall automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month periods."
   - Rationale: 60 days balances procurement planning vs. Redwood capacity scheduling; it's what Neha offered.

2) Termination for Convenience (Order Form): 
   - For Order Forms with total annualized commitment < $50,000 USD: Finovate may terminate for convenience with thirty (30) days' prior written notice; Redwood shall refund any prepaid, unused fees on a pro-rata basis within thirty (30) days less an administrative fee of up to five percent (5%).
   - For Order Forms with total annualized commitment >= $50,000 USD: Finovate may terminate for convenience with sixty (60) days' prior written notice; in such cases Redwood shall either (i) refund prepaid, unused fees on a pro-rata basis less an administrative fee of up to five percent (5%), or (ii) charge a termination amount equal to the actual costs of reserved capacity provisioning for the remaining notice period, at Redwood's discretion.
   - Rationale: protects Redwood from capacity and multi-month provisioning costs while offering clear economics and a cap on administrative fees.

3) Transition Support: Redwood will provide a standard Transition Runbook and one (1) operational handoff call during the notice period for enterprise Order Forms. Additional migration work will be quoted separately.

4) Audit / Evidence: Any refund calculation will be accompanied by a brief statement of calculation and invoice.

If Finovate would like to remove the termination amount option for larger commitments in favor of an absolute pro-rata refund (minus admin fee), we're open to that as a commercial concession but would ask for a modest one-time setup fee or slight rate adjustment to offset allocation risk.

Next steps: Neha — please confirm if we should offer the full clause above or the simplified variant (pro-rata refund only) as the commercial concession. Jill — if you can give us a thumbs up on either option, I'll prepare a DocuSign-ready Order Form with the chosen language.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

--- Attachment: MSA_redline_karthik_v2.docx (legal redline, annotated)

From: Jill Park <procurement@finovate.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Finovate Legal <legal@finovate.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify renewal mechanics & termination-for-convenience carveout — proposed legal language

Neha / Karthik — thanks for the clear options and Karthik's language. Procurement and our legal team discussed internally. We can accept the 60-day opt-out window for annual auto-renewals. For termination for convenience on enterprise commitments, we prefer a single, simple economic outcome: pro-rata refund of unused prepaid months less a flat administrative fee (we propose 3%), and no separate "termination amount" catalogue tied to reserved capacity. It's important for our CFO to have predictable exit economics.

If Redwood is willing to accept the pro-rata refund minus a 3% admin fee (instead of the 5% you proposed) for >= $50k commitments, Finovate can sign the Order Form this week. Please prepare a DocuSign link with the Order Form that incorporates the agreed clause and the agreed deal id (FN-45321). We anticipate signature by EOD Thursday once DocuSign is received.

Thanks — Jill
Jill Park
Head of Procurement — Finovate Inc.
